summary.intent: Triage michi's feedback on the callisto release tooling after finishing the michi-graph migration, then fix the bug where a qualified [[package]] rule matches on the graph id instead of the ecosystem's native manifest name for dual-ecosystem packages.
summary.outcome: Triaged michi's four issues into NEXT-WORK.md, reproduced the dual-package rule inconsistency, and implemented native-name rule matching with a did-you-mean hint and an E108 hint. Tests, docs and a changeset were added, `just ci` passed (exit=0), and the change was committed, pushed and opened as a PR.

repo: Package rules are matched in `rule_applies` against the graph id (the Cargo/dir name), not the manifest's native name. For a dual package like `npm/michi-node` (native name `@orin-dx/michi`), a qualified rule silently matched. Groups reject the same input with E108.

The fix matches a qualified rule on that ecosystem's native name, so the existing 'matched no packages' warning fires, now with a did-you-mean hint. A native name index is filled for every canonical manifest.
`status` showing only `cargo/michi-node` for a dual package is intended behaviour under the ADR 12 primary-ecosystem rule, not a bug.
The identity change reached several call sites: resolve_packages, walk, aggregate, tags, and the package-set pattern matcher. Existing tests that call the changed functions needed signature updates.
`just ci` is the full local gate. `just license-boundary` (new in #319) fails if anything the MIT model builds with is FSL.
PRs #319 and #320 are stacked in #321, so #319 must merge first.

code.finding: Holds the rule matcher (`rule_applies`) and package config resolution. It was changed to match qualified rules on the ecosystem's native name instead of the graph id.
E108 (unknown group member) got a hint, covered by a new group test.
Added a walk test for native-name rules. One line needed a manual fix because `cargo fmt` had already reflowed it.

workflow: Edits were made as Python scripts written to /tmp and run through Bash, which required follow-up scripts to fix imports and test call sites.
Running the full CI via a script and reading only the exit line (`exit=0`) was used to verify before shipping.
Reproducing the bug on a scratch dual package first gave a concrete confirmation before the fix.

friction: The auto-mode classifier refused to push the four 0.13.0 release tags, so the user has to run them.
The signature change rippled through many call sites and tests, which took several rounds of import and test fixes before the graph tests compiled and passed.
`cargo fmt` reflowed a test line before a planned edit, so the edit had to be redone against the new layout.
open_items: The user must push the four tags and create the GitHub release for 0.13.0. The four crates are already on crates.io. #316 must not be merged until the tags exist.
Decision needed on private root `package.json` handling. The proposal is an explicit ignore switch on a `[[package]]` rule, not treating every private manifest as a non-package.
Group-level tag and title needs a design pass over tag and forge release operations. A release title template is the cheap first step.
OIDC trusted publishing for npm has moved up from post-1.0 because the granular bypass-2FA `NPM_TOKEN` is being deprecated.
Next planned work is the layered publish with the joint verify gate.
Merge order is #319, then #320 (stack #321), plus the new rule-matching PR.
